title: A service registry without check-then-act

blocks.text: The page's `UnsafeRegistry` does `if (!containsKey(name)) put(name, endpoint)` on a `HashMap`: a check-then-act race on a map that is not thread-safe. Its fix uses `ConcurrentHashMap` and one **atomic** call instead of two, and the page's best practices prefer `computeIfAbsent` to a manual check-then-act, because its function runs **at most once per key**.
Write `ServiceRegistry`, safe to use from many threads:

items: `register(name, endpoint)` adds the service and returns `true`, or returns `false` and changes nothing when the name is already registered.
`unregister(name)` removes it and returns whether it was there.

`resolve(name, resolver)` returns the endpoint for `name`, calling `resolver.apply(name)` to find it when it is not registered yet, and registering the result. Two threads resolving the same unknown name at once call the resolver **once**.

rows: `false`, once that resolve ends; `lookup("billing")` is the resolved endpoint

cases.says: register, lookup, unregister and names keep a map of service names to endpoints.
Registering a name that is already there returns false and keeps the first endpoint.
Two threads resolving the same unknown name at the same time make the resolver run exactly once, and both get its endpoint.
register() of a name that a resolve is registering at that moment returns false and leaves the resolved endpoint in place: its check and its insert are one step.

origin.section: 4. Using HashMap in concurrent contexts instead of ConcurrentHashMap

concepts: A shared map needs ConcurrentHashMap and one atomic call such as putIfAbsent, never a containsKey-then-put.
ConcurrentHashMap.computeIfAbsent runs its mapping function at most once per key, even under concurrent access.
